title: Are the points of a six pointed star equilateral?
description: A six pointed star with a regular hexagon inside it. At each corner of the hexagon a straight line leaves sixty degrees for the triangle, so every point has three sixty degree angles. Keeko's doubt, taking the hexagon angle for the point angle, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angle of the point triangle and the hexagon angle share a straight line, so they add to one hundred and eighty. Watch for students who read the point angle as the hexagon angle.

source: A six-pointed star has outer points A, B, C, D, E, F and an
video_script.why: The child finds the angles of a point of the star and uses them to say what kind of triangle it is.
video_script.substitution: Each point sits on the extended sides of the hexagon, so its base angles are 180 minus 120.
video_script.anchor: A six pointed star with outer points A, B, C, D, E, F and an inner regular hexagon G, H, I, J, K, L.
video_script.wrong_answer: the same angle as the hexagon
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads angle AGH as the same angle as the hexagon, so it would be 120 degrees. But angle AGH and angle LGH lie on a straight line and add to 180 degrees, so angle AGH is 60 degrees.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, each point of the star is an equilateral triangle.

final_answer.value: Yes, each point of the star is an equilateral triangle
final_answer.spoken: yes, each point of the star is an equilateral triangle

hold_back: each point of the star is an equilateral triangle
maths_rules: GHIJKL is a regular hexagon, so each of its angles is 120°.
AG lies along the extended side LG and AH along the extended side IH.
The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so ∠GAH = 180° − 60° − 60° = 60°.
All three angles are 60°, so triangle AGH is equilateral; the same reasoning works for the other five points.
Slip: reading ∠AGH as the hexagon angle 120°.
video_script.design: One star, one regular hexagon inside it. The point triangle AGH is shaded and its angles filled in one by one. The slip is the hexagon angle taken for the point angle.
